title: The N-run shortcut in find_lcp returns an LCP above max_query_len
body:
`find_lcp` in `libsufr/src/build/sort.rs` returns early when both suffixes start inside a run of N: the LCP is the shorter remaining run, `min(end1 - start1, end2 - start2)`. That return never consults `max_query_len`, so with `-a` (N suffixes kept) and `-m` the LCP array holds values up to the run length. The same defect on the other path of the function, where `max_query_len` replaced `len`, is sufr-2b76b5.

Measured with the binary at c9c880d on `data/inputs/long_dna_sequence.fa`, which has a run of 2000 N:

| build | rows with LCP above 3 |
|---|---|
| `--dna -m 3 --write-lcp` | 13, all 4 or 5, from sufr-2b76b5 |
| `--dna -a -m 3 --write-lcp` | 987, values up to the run length |

After the sufr-2b76b5 fix the second build still has 975 rows above 3, all from this return.

## Proposal

Cap the shortcut's result at `max_query_len` when it is nonzero, in the plain form, and a unit test in `test_find_lcp_no_seed_mask`: text `NNNNA`, suffixes 0 and 1, `n_ranges` `[0..4]`, `max_query_len` 2, expecting 2 where the code gives 3 today. The check from sufr-2b76b5 applies: every adjacent LCP recomputed from the suffix text and capped must agree with the file on the `-a -m 3` build.

## Cost

The `.sufr` bytes of a build with `-a` and `-m` on a text with runs of 1000 N or more change in the LCP array and may change in the order inside groups of equal keys, as the sufr-2b76b5 fix did. No fixture is built with `-m`.
